concepts.def: Snapshots of audio per second. CD = 44.1 kHz.
The source of sound in a synthesizer.
Attack, Decay, Sustain, Release — shape of a note.
Final polish — overall EQ, loudness, format prep.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Digital audio is just thousands of snapshots per second. Sample rate = how often (44.1 kHz on CDs means 44,100 snapshots/sec). Bit depth = how detailed each snapshot is (16-bit on CDs).

Higher sample rates (96 kHz) and bit depths (24-bit) are common in studios, then downsampled for release.

A synthesizer starts with an oscillator generating a waveform — sine, square, sawtooth, triangle. Filters then shape the tone, and an ADSR envelope shapes the volume over time.

Attack: how fast it starts. Decay: how it drops. Sustain: the held level. Release: how it fades after the note ends.

Mastering is the last stage before release — applied to the finished stereo mix. The mastering engineer balances overall tone with EQ, raises perceived volume with a limiter, and ensures the track sits well next to commercial releases.

They also create the right format (44.1 kHz/16-bit WAV for CDs/streaming) and add metadata.
